correctness.rationale: The unique central letter excludes all proper borders longer than Z_(k-1); the shorter ones reduce recursively. Among prefixes of the smaller word, precisely its borders can gain the central letter as a successor. Induction therefore gives the stated extension sets and at most one possible successor for any other prefix. An absent word containing the new letter internally just once would be forced to occur by the prefix and suffix being anchored at that same unique position. Two copies can only be the endpoints, where the middle is exactly a border (including the empty one); a single endpoint copy instead requires a noninitial successor of a Zimin prefix. This exhausts the alternatives, includes k=1, and gives k-j diagonal and (k-j-1)(k-j-2) ordered off-diagonal terms at length 2^j+1.
residual_risks: The exact alphabet and linear contiguous factors are essential; the bounded reproduction does not replace the induction.
